letter.subject: Concern about cookie and tracking practices on angloamerican.com following rejection of cookies
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified on https://angloamerican.com during an automated, passive audit carried out on 2026-11-08 04:09 UTC. Using a fresh browser, we visited the site, clicked the cookie banner’s “Reject All” option, then browsed the following pages and recorded what was still sent: https://www.angloamerican.com/our-portfolio, https://www.angloamerican.com/sustainability-strategy, and https://www.angloamerican.com/futuresmart/futuresmart-mining. We also reviewed your privacy policy at https://www.angloamerican.com/site-services/privacy-policy.

The issues we ask you to explain are:

1. Our review suggests marketing cookies were set despite the site’s stated controls. After “Reject All” was clicked, new YouTube cookies containing apparent unique identifiers were set while the site was browsed. Your policy says: “You can control which types of cookie are set by changing your preferences through our cookie banner when you first visit our website or at any time by using the preference table below:”. It also classifies YouTube __Secure-* cookies as marketing cookies.

2. After rejection, Google still received data: 45 requests to doubleclick.net, google-analytics.com, googletagmanager.com, and youtube.com. New cookies set after rejection were VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, VISITOR_PRIVACY_METADATA, YSC, __Secure-ROLLOUT_TOKEN, and __Secure-YNID.

3. After rejection, Facebook still received data: 6 requests to facebook.net.

4. Scripts from google.com used WebGL (GPU model) fingerprinting after rejection, via https://www.google.com/js/th/n_BHgtbTP3l_ff810bu_K6lL5wb_ZK3aoRJMIVk8Tks.js.

5. Your privacy policy names 0 companies. We observed Facebook and Google and found no mention of them. We recognise the policy may describe recipients only by category.

6. Our review suggests the privacy policy does not cover two items anywhere in the version we read: your rights and the right to complain to the ICO.

Please:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential tracking that occurs without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
